prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: PR-09, Scene 2 isolated story prop. Style: Non-realistic 2.5D wartime illustration with a simplified low-poly appearance. Use broad angular planes, clean polygonal silhouettes, restrained human proportions and economical facial features. Apply muted olive, khaki, grey-green, earth brown and subdued warm skin tones. Materials are matte, with sparse texture and two or three broad shading tones. Keep outlines subtle and helmet shadows simple. Build depth through overlapping, separately layered foreground, middle-ground and background artwork. Preserve each character’s silhouette, costume and proportions across poses. Keep the mood quiet, human and sombre.
Generate one small hand-carved wooden toy horse with muted brick-red paint and ONE broken front leg. The horse faces left in a shallow three-quarter side view. The nearest front leg immediately below its chest is snapped off with a short angular raw-wood stub. Exactly three other legs remain attached, clearly distinguishable in silhouette. Place the one detached red leg piece beside the horse with a small transparent gap, below and to the left of the broken stub. Plain carved mane and tail, small restrained painted eye. No rocking base, wheels, saddle, ornate details, gore or real animal anatomy. Broad simple flat planes, matte paint, sparse angular wear marks showing warm brown wood at edges. No realistic woodgrain noise, no excessive tiny polygon facets.
Entire horse and detached leg visible with generous transparent margins; square framing; neutral diffuse base lighting. Genuine transparent background, no floor, dust bed, scene, cast-shadow plane, label or text. Do not generate the snowflake; it will be a programmatic effect. This is one static image state for a 2.5D animation.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: PR-11 dining table and place settings, separate Scene 2 cutout. Style: Non-realistic 2.5D wartime illustration with a simplified low-poly appearance. Use broad angular planes, clean polygonal silhouettes, restrained human proportions and economical facial features. Apply muted olive, khaki, grey-green, earth brown and subdued warm skin tones. Generate one modest old farmhouse dining table of warm medium-brown wood, four straight simple legs, rectangular tabletop, shown in a mild elevated three-quarter view. It is set for EXACTLY four people: four separate matte off-white plates, two at the far long edge and two at the near long edge, each with a minimal knife/spoon beside it. Include one simple off-white cup tipped on its side near a plate. No food, people, hands, other furniture or chairs in this image. The child chair is a separate asset. The empty settings should feel quietly abandoned, not theatrically destroyed. Simple plank divisions, a few broad wear marks, two or three main tonal planes per material. Sparse texture; no photoreal woodgrain, shiny metal or dense polygon noise.
Wide landscape composition; all four table legs and complete tabletop within the frame with generous margins. Genuine transparent background, no room, floor, ground shadow, haze or labels. Neutral diffuse base lighting, not baked kitchen warmth or blue exterior grade. No ash particles yet; ash will be a separate programmatic layer. Four plates must be visible and countable. One image only, no contact sheet.

Warm medium-brown matte wood, straight square legs, modest slatted back with three simple vertical slats, no decorative carvings, no high-chair tray, no wheels. Child-sized ordinary chair. Mild elevated three-quarter front view matching an elevated farmhouse table view; all legs, cushion and back visible. Portrait composition with entire chair visible and generous transparent margins. Genuine transparent background. No table, toys, child, hands, other furniture, floor, ash, cast-shadow plane, words or labels. Neutral diffuse lighting. This is a single still prop for programmatic placement and parallax.

Use case: compositing. Asset type: PR-24 completed rifle-and-helmet grave marker, one isolated static cutout for Scene 2. Input image 1 is the established rifle design reference. Preserve its walnut-brown stock, dark matte metal and olive canvas sling in the new orientation. Style: Non-realistic 2.5D wartime illustration with a simplified low-poly appearance. Use broad angular planes, clean polygonal silhouettes, restrained human proportions and economical facial features. Apply muted olive, khaki, grey-green, earth brown and subdued warm skin tones. Materials are matte, with sparse texture and two or three broad shading tones. Keep outlines subtle and helmet shadows simple. Build depth through overlapping, separately layered foreground, middle-ground and background artwork. Preserve each character’s silhouette, costume and proportions across poses. Create ONE completed marker: the reference M1 Garand stands vertically upside down, buttstock at the top and barrel pointing downward, with a simple fixed bayonet extending from the muzzle toward the bottom. A muted olive US M1 steel helmet rests naturally over the upturned buttstock. The canvas sling hangs vertically beside the rifle. Show the complete marker from helmet crown to bayonet tip in a shallow three-quarter side view. The grounded placement will happen in composition, so do not add soil. The helmet has a simple rounded dome and short rim, matte finish, no symbols. Keep the rifle identifiable and simplify secondary surface detail into broad polygonal shapes. The marker is a sombre sign of a burial, not a weapon action scene.
Tall portrait composition with ample transparent margins. Genuine transparent background, no people or hands, no planting animation, no earth mound, boots, crosses, plaques, flowers, dog tags, text or extra markers. Neutral diffuse lighting. Return only one static marker; it will be instanced three times in the animation.
